reason: A is the better, testable intervention because Cr–Al oxidation can plausibly develop a protective alumina-containing scale while reducing interfacial transport, although the Al level, scale location, and exposure durations require refinement. B is physically untenable over its stated 1200–1600°C range because Inconel 718 approaches or exceeds melting and Ni can react strongly with Zr, potentially forming low-melting phases rather than a stable diffusion barrier; its cited evidence also does not support this specific Cr/Ni-alloy/Zr system.
